nodes.summary: The decision problem 3-MACHINE FLOW SHOP SCHEDULING accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of flow-shop instances, to an instance that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: The 3-machine flow shop scheduling decision problem

nodes.summary: Let an instance consist of jobs $1, \dots, n$, where job $j$ is a list of natural numbers whose $k$-th entry $p_{j,k}$ is its processing time on machine $k$ (read as $0$ if the list has fewer than $k$ entries), and a deadline $D$. The instance is feasible when there are natural numbers $s_{j,k}$, for each job $j$ and each $k \in \{1, 2, 3\}$, such that for every job $j$ we have $s_{j,1} + p_{j,1} \le s_{j,2}$,…
nodes.title: Feasible flow-shop schedules

nodes.summary: A flow-shop instance is a pair consisting of a finite list of jobs, each a finite list of natural numbers (its processing times on machines 1, 2 and 3, in that order), and a natural number $D$, the deadline. The type does not force a job to have exactly three entries; that is part of well-formedness.
nodes.title: Flow-shop instances

nodes.summary: The 3-machine flow shop scheduling decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: 3-MACHINE FLOW SHOP SCHEDULING is NP-complete

nodes.summary: A flow-shop instance is well formed when every job in it is a list of exactly three natural numbers.
nodes.title: Well-formed flow-shop instances

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
